newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts helped by weather - NOV 8.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts helped by weather - NOV 8.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Friday in a lackluster session, with front months underpinned by forecasts for some colder East Coast and Midwest weather next week, industry sources said.
December gained 2.6 cents to close at $2.669 per million British thermal units. January settled up the same amount at $2.675. Other deferreds ended narrowly mixed.

"Any sign of cold and the market is going to move (up). Early in the season, the market is going to be very sensitive to weather," said one East Coast trader. But he said any return to milder temperatures should quickly rouse the bears.
Northeast and Midwest temperatures are expected to be well-below normal early next week, but much of the rest of the country will be normal to above-normal.
Technically, traders said the market was range bound, with good support in December still in the $2.52-2.53 area and resistance at $2.745 and then at the $2.88 contract high.

Cash sources said weekend Gulf Coast prices held relatively steady Friday at about $2.70. Midwest pipes also were unchanged in the high-$2.50s. Colder weekend weather forecasts drove New York city gate gas prices up a dime or more to the $3.05-3.15 range.

The 12-month Henry Hub strip climbed 0.6 cent to $2.171. NYMEX Alberta natgas did not trade Friday but December closed two cents higher at a new contract high of $1.29, while deferreds settled up by two to 3.5 cents.
NYMEX Permian natgas also was untraded. December ended unchanged at $2.49, while other months closed down by one-half to one cent.

On the KCBT, December finished one-half cent lower at $2.485, while deferreds settled down the same amount. The East/West spread widened by 3.1 cents to 18.4 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 30 contracts traded, down sharply from Thursday's total of 364.
